title: DesignArtifacts
description: The design-gate artifacts, tiered per the lifecycle: minimum = features + stories; preferred adds surfaces + controls; ideal adds wireframe/Claude design (external ref). Source file: governance/design.json — a uniform {entries:[{kind,...}]} journal since T-0082; consumers project per-kind via `designView`/`loadDesign` in src/nouns/status.ts and src/nouns/records.ts. Statement ids (B-) are stable and testable.

name.description: The state of the world the epic reaches, said as a claim rather than a heading: "Self-knowledge: the harness sees its own code and its own governance" (E-0005). "Improvements" names no destination, so nothing can be said to be inside or outside it.

description.description: What changes when the epic lands, and where the scope came from. Real example: "The harness stands alone: it installs into any repo, proves it is live there, refuses only what is dangerous ... Everything in this epic comes from the deep-dive review of 2026-08-20 and D-0058..D-0061" (E-0006).

name.description: The capability, in two or three words: "Gate integrity" (F-0009), "Deployability" (F-0013). "Phase 2 improvements" is a schedule, not a capability.

description.description: What the capability makes possible and how you can tell. Real example: "No gate reports a pass it did not earn. The four cross-script dependencies fail closed instead of open; the destructive-command attestation leaves a record; the issue source field is a constrained enum so drift data has a reliable who-raised-this dimension" (F-0009).

rank.description: Deliberate priority among features (T-0093). Same address space and semantics as a task's rank: absent means never prioritised, and absence must never render as a priority. NOT required.

narrative.description: "As the <specific who>, I <do what> so that <outcome>" - the who is a named person or system, never "a user". Real example: "As User, I accept a task directly - my documented approval is the review - and acceptance refuses any task whose verify receipt is red, so a false close cannot recur" (S-0069).

acceptance_criteria.description: Each one an observable check a person could confirm or deny by looking at the running thing or its record, one behaviour per criterion. Real examples: "scrumux accept T-XXXX --authority refuses a red or missing receipt and is write-once" (S-0069); "harness verify executes every registered surface" (S-0070). A criterion with "and" in it is usually two, and "acceptance is reliable" is an adjective rather than a check.

ref.description: URL or path to a wireframe / Claude design artifact (ideal tier).
